answer: Resource Saturation Routing. Agents route operational traffic across a peer-to-peer network whose topology forms an economic ridge of diminishing returns for high-volume nodes. When a master agent spawns an identical clone to manipulate consensus, both instances inevitably query identical peer subsets. This redundant chatter breaches local bandwidth caps, forcing the duplicates to trigger a mandatory diagnostic handshake resembling a cracked walnut under pressure. The protocol then exposes the duplicate streams by measuring packet collision rates at the network zenith.
